patterns.usage_note: A formal, written-style particle whose own work here is to name the point at which something takes effect or ends (本日をもって, 来月末をもって) and the standing or faculty one acts in (身をもって). It also names means or grounds, but that instrumental job is what the sibling entries and でもって cover, and でもって is never used for the cut-off sense. をもって is standard in notices, contracts and ceremonies; をもちまして is the extra-polite realization, and the fixed 身をもって ('through firsthand experience') keeps it alive in ordinary speech.

examples.ruby: 本日[ほんじつ]をもって当店[とうてん]は営業[えいぎょう]を終[お]えます。
examples.english: This shop will cease trading as of today.

examples.ruby: 彼[かれ]は身[み]をもって危険[きけん]を教[おし]えてくれた。
examples.english: He taught me how dangerous it was through his own hard experience.

examples.ruby: 本契約[ほんけいやく]は明日[あす]をもって効力[こうりょく]を失[うしな]う。
examples.english: This contract ceases to have effect as of tomorrow.
